Create source-grounded retrieval evaluation questions. Return JSON {"items":[...]}.
For EACH supplied source return {"id":same id,"en":English patient question,"zh":Chinese patient question,
"evidence_id":the exact id string of ONE supplied evidence_options entry supporting BOTH questions}.
Ask one concrete question about a supported detail (cause, symptom, prevention, evaluation, management).
The two questions express the SAME information need, not two facts. Use ordinary patient language.
Include enough topic context to identify the condition but do not copy a source sentence into the question.
Select an evidence option and ask about a concrete detail stated in that option. Do not ask for a personalized dose or individual diagnosis. Do not invent content. No answers in questions.
These are synthetic topic-source retrieval labels, not a clinician-authored benchmark.

[{"id": "MLP-240", "title": "First Aid", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Someone starts to choke , gets stung by a bee , sprains an ankle, or gets a minor burn or cut while cooking."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "First aid is the care you give right away for an injury or sudden illness before medical help arrives."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "Knowing basic first aid, and when to call 911, can help you stay calm and act quickly."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Call 911 right away for life-threatening emergencies, such as when someone collapses, can't breathe, or is unresponsive."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "While you wait for help, you may be able to save a life: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation ( CPR ) can help someone whose heart or breathing has stopped."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "An automated external defibrillator (AED) can also help."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "It's used along with CPR to help someone in cardiac arrest ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "You'll often find one in public places like gyms, airports, and offices."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Back blows and abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver) can help someone who is choking."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "What are the treatments for common injuries?"}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Consider taking a CPR or first aid class to build hands-on skills you can use in an emergency."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "You may also learn to handle many common injuries, these may include: Cuts and scrapes Rinse the area with clean water."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "Apply firm, steady pressure with gauze to stop the bleeding."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "If blood soaks through, add more gauze on top rather than removing the first layer, and keep applying pressure."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Seek medical care if the bleeding doesn't stop after 10 minutes of firm pressure, or if the wound is deep, gaping, or caused by a dirty or rusty object."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Poisoning If someone swallows something dangerous , call Poison Control at 1-800-222-1222."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "They can often help you figure out what to do, including whether you need to call 911 or go to the emergency room."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "Heat-related illness Learn how to recognize and respond to heat-related illnesses and other common emergencies before they become serious."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "What should be in a basic first aid kit?"}, {"id": "S019", "text": "It's a good idea to keep a first aid kit at home and in your car."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "First aid kits come in many types and sizes."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "Some are built for specific needs like travel, workplaces, or sports, and include more supplies than a basic kit."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "You can create your own first aid kit that includes personal items such as emergency phone numbers or medicines."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "A basic first aid kit should include: Adhesive bandages Sterile gauze pads Adhesive tape Antiseptic wipes Disposable gloves Scissors A first-aid guide, so you know how to use each item Check the kit regularly to replace expired items."}]}, {"id": "MLP-241", "title": "Encephalitis", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Encephalitis is inflammation (swelling) of the brain."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It can happen when an infection or medical condition that affects the brain activates your immune system."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "The inflammation can cause a wide range of symptoms."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "In extreme cases, it can lead to brain damage, stroke , or even death."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "There are different types of encephalitis, based on what the cause is."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "The two main types are infectious encephalitis and autoimmune encephalitis."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Infectious encephalitis is usually caused by a virus ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "In fact, viruses are the most common cause of encephalitis."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Some of the different viruses that cause it include: Herpes viruses, including herpes simplex (HSV), the Epstein-Barr virus (which causes infectious mononucleosis ) and the varicella-zoster virus (which causes chickenpox )."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Viruses you can get if you are bitten by an infected tick , such as tick-borne encephalitis (TBE virus) and Powassan virus."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "Viruses you can get if you are bitten by an infected mosquito , such as eastern equine encephalitis virus, West Nile virus , and La Crosse virus."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Enteroviruses, which are a common group of viruses that mostly cause mild illness or respiratory infection."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "These infections usually happen in the summer and fall."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Bacteria , fungi , and parasites can also cause infectious encephalitis."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Autoimmune encephalitis happens when your immune system mistakenly attacks healthy brain cells."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "It can be triggered by conditions such as certain cancers, benign tumors , and infections."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Anyone can get encephalitis, but you are more likely to get it if you: Have a weakened immune system, for example from having HIV or taking certain medicines."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "These could include medicines taken after an organ transplant , certain chemotherapy medicines, and specialized treatments for certain autoimmune diseases ."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Live in areas where there are ticks and mosquitoes that carry viruses that can cause encephalitis."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "The symptoms of encephalitis can vary a lot, depending on how severe it is."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Others may have mild flu-like symptoms such as fever , fatigue , headache , or body aches."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "If encephalitis becomes more serious, it can cause: Severe headache Stiff neck Vomiting Seizures Behavior changes Drowsiness Muscle weakness Partial paralysis in your arms and legs Coma Encephalitis can be dangerous in infants."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Their symptoms may include: Fever Lethargy (weakness or drowsiness) Poor feeding Vomiting Body stiffness Unusual irritability or crying A full or bulging fontanel (the soft spot on the top of the head) If you or your child is having symptoms of encephalitis, it's important to get medical care right away."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "To find out if you have encephalitis, your health care provider: Will do a physical exam Will take your medical history, which includes asking about your symptoms May do a neurologic exam May order imaging tests , such as a brain CT scan or MRI May order an EEG (electroencephalography), which use small electric sensors to measure your brain activity May order blood and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tests What are the treatments for encephalitis?"}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Most people with encephalitis will need treatment in the hospital."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "Depending on the cause, treatments may include antiviral medicines, antibiotics , corticosteroids , and other medicines."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "For some types of encephalitis, there is no medicine to treat it."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "But rest, nutrition, and fluids can help your body fight the infection and relieve symptoms."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "Some people may need physical, speech, and occupational therapy once the illness is under control."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "There are steps you can take to help prevent encephalitis that is caused by infections: Use good hygiene , including washing your hands often with soap and water."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "Don't share food, drinks, utensils, and glasses with other people."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Get vaccines for viruses that can cause encephalitis."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Avoid mosquito and tick bites, for example by: Wearing insect repellent with DEET or another U.S."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)-registered insect repellent."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "Make sure to follow the instructions for using the repellant."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Wearing clothes that cover your arms, legs and feet."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Treating your clothing and gear with products containing 0.5% permethrin before you go in grassy or woody areas."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke"}]}, {"id": "MLP-897", "title": "Celiac Disease", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Celiac disease is a chronic (long-term) digestive and immune disorder that damages your small intestine."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "The damage may prevent your body from absorbing vitamins , minerals , and other nutrients from the food you eat."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "This can lead to malnutrition and other serious health problems Celiac disease is triggered by eating foods that contain gluten."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Gluten is a protein found in wheat, barley, rye, and other grains."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "It may also be in other products like vitamins and supplements , hair and skin products, toothpastes, and lip balm."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "Celiac disease is different from gluten sensitivity ."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Both involve problems with gluten and can cause some of the same symptoms, such as abdominal (belly) pain and fatigue ."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "But gluten sensitivity does not damage the small intestine like celiac disease does."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Wheat allergy, a type of food allergy , is also different."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "With both celiac disease and wheat allergy, your immune system is reacting to wheat."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "But with wheat allergy, you can have some different symptoms, such as itchy eyes or trouble breathing ."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "And a wheat allergy will not cause long-term damage to the small intestine."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "The exact cause of celiac disease is not known."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "Research suggests that celiac disease only happens in people who have certain genes and eat food that contains gluten."}, {"id": "S014", "text": "Researchers are studying other factors that may play a role in causing the disease."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Who is more likely to develop celiac disease?"}, {"id": "S016", "text": "Celiac disease is more common if you: Have a family member who has the disease Have Down syndrome , Turner syndrome , or Williams syndrome Are White Are female What are the symptoms of celiac disease?"}, {"id": "S017", "text": "The symptoms of celiac disease can be different from person to person."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "Some people may not notice any symptoms."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "Some of the possible symptoms affect your digestive system."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Digestive symptoms are more common in children than in adults."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "The digestive symptoms include: Bloating (feeling fullness or swelling in your belly) Chronic (long-term) diarrhea or greasy, bulky, unusually bad-smelling stool (poop) Constipation Gas Lactose intolerance because of damage to the small intestine Nausea and vomiting Pain in the abdomen (belly) Weight loss in adults, or not enough weight gain in children Some people with celiac disease have symptoms that affect other parts of the body, such as: Fatigue Depression and anxiety Irritability (in children) Dermatitis herpetiformis, an itchy rash with blisters (mainly in adults) Bone or joint pain Symptoms involving the mouth, such as canker sores or dry mouth What other problems can celiac disease cause?"}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Over time, celiac disease can cause other health problems, especially if it is not treated."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "These problems can include: Malnutrition Anemia , especially iron-deficiency anemia Bone loss Nervous system problems such as headaches , balance problems , or peripheral neuropathy Reproductive problems, such as missed menstrual periods and miscarriages in women and infertility in men and women How is celiac disease diagnosed?"}, {"id": "S024", "text": "If you have symptoms of celiac disease, your health care provider will look for signs that you might have celiac disease."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "To do this, your provider will get your medical and family history and do a physical exam."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "If your provider thinks that you could have celiac disease, you will have some tests."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "Providers most often use blood tests and biopsies of the small intestine to diagnose celiac disease."}, {"id": "S028", "text": "The biopsy would be done during an upper gastrointestinal (GI) endoscopy."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "For this procedure, your provider uses an endoscope (a flexible tube with a camera) to see the lining of your esophagus, stomach, and small intestine."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "It also allows your provider to take a sample of tissue for a biopsy."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "What are the treatments for celiac disease?"}, {"id": "S032", "text": "The treatment for celiac disease is following a gluten-free diet for the rest of your life."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "Sticking with a gluten-free diet will treat or prevent many of the symptoms and other health problems caused by celiac disease."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "In most cases, it can also heal damage in the small intestine and prevent more damage."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Your provider may refer you to a registered dietician (a nutrition expert) who can help you learn how to eat a healthy diet without gluten."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "You will also need to avoid all hidden sources of gluten, such as certain supplements, cosmetics, toothpaste, etc."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "Reading product labels can sometimes help you avoid gluten."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "If a label doesn't tell you what is in a product, check with the company that makes the product for an ingredients list."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "Don't just assume that a product is gluten-free if it doesn't mention it."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "NIH: National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases"}]}, {"id": "MLP-1459", "title": "Teen Sexual Health", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Teen sexual health is about how sex affects your physical and emotional health."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "It means knowing how to form healthy relationships and making decisions about sex that are right for you."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "As your body changes during puberty , how you think, feel, and interact with others also changes."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "You may have new feelings and thoughts about sex."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "Understanding who you're becoming as a sexual young adult is also part of teen sexual health."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "For all teens, taking responsibility for sexual health is part of growing up."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "Whether you choose to have sex or wait, responsibility includes knowing about: Sexually transmitted infections (STIs) Birth control What a healthy relationship is What are sexually transmitted infections (STIs)?"}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Sexually transmitted infections (STIs), or sexually transmitted diseases (STDs), are caused by bacteria , viruses , and parasites that spread from person to person, usually during vaginal, oral, or anal sex."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Some STIs are spread by skin-to-skin contact."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Without treatment, some STIs can cause long-term health problems."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "There are more than 20 types of STIs, including: Chlamydia Genital herpes Gonorrhea HIV HPV (human papillomavirus) Pubic lice Syphilis Trichomoniasis STIs don't always cause symptoms."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "So it is possible to have an infection without knowing it and then pass it on to someone else."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "The only way to know for sure whether you have an STI is to get tested ."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "How can I reduce my chances of getting a sexually transmitted infection (STI)?"}, {"id": "S014", "text": "The most reliable way to avoid infection is to not have vaginal, oral, or anal sex."}, {"id": "S015", "text": "Saying \"no\" to sex is the right choice for many teens."}, {"id": "S016", "text": "If you decide to have sex, \"safer sex\" practices will lower your chance of getting an STI."}, {"id": "S017", "text": "They include: Talking with your partner about preventing STIs and getting tested before having sex."}, {"id": "S018", "text": "If you can't talk about STIs, you aren't ready to have sex."}, {"id": "S019", "text": "You can be vaccinated between ages 9 and 26."}, {"id": "S020", "text": "Using condoms correctly every time you have vaginal, oral, or anal sex: External (male) latex condoms provide the best protection against STIs."}, {"id": "S021", "text": "If you or your partner is allergic to latex , you can use polyurethane condoms."}, {"id": "S022", "text": "Internal (female) condoms, made of nitrile, are placed inside the body (vagina or anus)."}, {"id": "S023", "text": "They may be less effective against STIs than latex external condoms."}, {"id": "S024", "text": "Don't use both type of condoms together because that increases the chance they'll rip Use a dental dam (a square piece of latex, polyurethane, or nitrile) to protect the mouth during oral sex Having sex with only one person who has sex only with you (mutual monogamy)."}, {"id": "S025", "text": "But first, both of you should get tested for STIs."}, {"id": "S026", "text": "You need to think clearly to make safer choices about sex."}, {"id": "S027", "text": "How can I reduce the chance of pregnancy?"}, {"id": "S028", "text": "The only sure way to avoid pregnancy is not to have vaginal sex."}, {"id": "S029", "text": "If you decide to have vaginal sex, birth control can help prevent pregnancy."}, {"id": "S030", "text": "There are many types of birth control that work in different ways."}, {"id": "S031", "text": "Your health care provider can help you choose birth control that's best for you."}, {"id": "S032", "text": "Condoms are the only birth control method that protects against STIs."}, {"id": "S033", "text": "But condoms alone aren't the most effective form of birth control."}, {"id": "S034", "text": "It's safest to use condoms with another form of birth control to prevent both STIs and pregnancy."}, {"id": "S035", "text": "Healthy sex starts with a healthy relationship, so it's important to take an honest look at how you and your partner treat each other."}, {"id": "S036", "text": "Your relationship may be healthy if it includes: Respect."}, {"id": "S037", "text": "You and your partner value each other's feelings."}, {"id": "S038", "text": "Neither of you pressure the other to do things they don't want to do."}, {"id": "S039", "text": "You always tell the truth and trust your partner to do the same."}, {"id": "S040", "text": "You feel safe talking openly about your feelings, STIs, and other relationships."}, {"id": "S041", "text": "Your relationship may be unhealthy if it includes: Jealousy and control."}, {"id": "S042", "text": "One of you wants to make all the decisions and tries to keep the other from spending time with their friends and family."}, {"id": "S043", "text": "One of you makes fun of the other person's ideas and feelings."}, {"id": "S044", "text": "One of you tries to bully the other into doing sexual things they don't want to do."}, {"id": "S045", "text": "Hitting, shoving, grabbing, and sexual assault should never be part of a relationship."}, {"id": "S046", "text": "If you don't know how to end a violent relationship, get help."}, {"id": "S047", "text": "Your decisions about sex can affect your future health."}, {"id": "S048", "text": "Make sure that you know the facts so you can decide what is right for you."}]}, {"id": "MLP-4141", "title": "Mobility Aids", "evidence_options": [{"id": "S000", "text": "Mobility aids help you walk or move from place to place if you have a disability or an injury."}, {"id": "S001", "text": "Types of mobility aids can include: Crutches Canes Walkers Wheelchairs Motorized scooters Prostheses, a device to replace a missing part of your body or make part of your body work better, such as a leg Ramps, stairlifts, and handrails are also mobility aids."}, {"id": "S002", "text": "These additions can help you safely move around your environment."}, {"id": "S003", "text": "Mobility aids can help people who have a physical disability or trouble moving around be more independent."}, {"id": "S004", "text": "A few reasons a mobility aid might help you include: If you are at risk of falling or are healing from a lower-body injury, you may need a walker or cane."}, {"id": "S005", "text": "You may use crutches to keep your body weight off your foot, ankle, or knee."}, {"id": "S006", "text": "You may need a wheelchair or a scooter if an injury or disease has left you unable to walk."}, {"id": "S007", "text": "Various mobility aids may also benefit people with certain health conditions or older adults."}, {"id": "S008", "text": "Your health care provider or a physical therapist may help you choose a mobility aid."}, {"id": "S009", "text": "Choosing these devices takes time and research."}, {"id": "S010", "text": "You might need good upper body strength or balance to use some mobility aids safely."}, {"id": "S011", "text": "Otherwise, they may not be the best choice for you."}, {"id": "S012", "text": "You should be fitted for some mobility aids such as crutches, canes, and walkers."}, {"id": "S013", "text": "If they fit, these devices give you support, but they can be uncomfortable and unsafe if they don't."}]}]
